headline: PM's flight from Japan delayed by nearly 5 hours due to spoiler glitch
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's return flight from Japan experienced a nearly five-hour delay at Narita International Airport after a Biman aircraft developed a fault in its spoiler system. Engineers deactivated the affected spoiler, allowing the PM and his en
details:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman

’s return flight from Japan was delayed by nearly five hours after the Biman aircraft carrying him and his entourage developed a fault in its spoiler system. The incident occurred before takeoff at Narita International Airport on the first day of the national carrier

’s newly introduced Thursday service.

The Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, Flight BG377, was scheduled to leave Narita at 3:00pm Bangladesh time but eventually took off at 7:55pm. It was expected to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 3:00am today.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines had recently increased its weekly flights between Dhaka and Narita from one to two, operating every Monday and Thursday. The Prime Minister was specifically returning home aboard this newly introduced Thursday flight.

Biman officials stated that the aircraft developed a fault in its No. 1 hydraulic spoiler after it began moving towards the runway. Spoilers are movable panels on an aircraft

’s wings that help reduce lift and control movement.

To resolve the issue, engineers deactivated the affected spoiler, allowing the Prime Minister and his delegation to return on the same aircraft. Biman clarified that no defects were found during pre-flight inspections, with the fault developing only after taxiing began.

Under the US Federal Aviation Administration

’s Master Minimum Equipment List for the Boeing 787, an aircraft can depart with one hydraulic spoiler inoperative. This is subject to specified conditions, including deactivation of the affected spoiler and checks before departure.

Sources from the Prime Minister

’s Office reported that the captain informed passengers of a technical problem five minutes after advancing towards the runway. The aircraft later returned to the parking apron, and passengers disembarked before the issue was resolved.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was traveling with his wife, Dr. Zubaida Rahman, and other delegation members. He was returning from a four-day official visit to Japan, held from October 26 to 29, at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

This is not the first time a Biman aircraft carrying a Bangladeshi prime minister has encountered technical problems. In 2016, a Biman Boeing 777-300ER carrying then-PM Sheikh Hasina made an emergency landing in Turkmenistan due to an engine oil-pressure problem.

Another incident occurred in April 2023 when a Biman Boeing 787 Dreamliner developed a weather radar malfunction while returning to Dhaka after dropping off Sheikh Hasina in Tokyo, though she was not aboard at the time of that specific fault.

headline_marked: [[UN grants Bangladesh 3-year LDC graduation deferment]] for smoother transition
headline: UN grants Bangladesh 3-year LDC graduation deferment for smoother transition
summary: The United Nations General Assembly has approved a three-year extension for Bangladesh's graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDCs) group, pushing the date to November 2029.
details: Bangladesh has secured a three-year extension for its graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDCs) group. This decision, made by world leaders at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, aims to ensure a smoother transition amidst global energy and supply chain disruptions.
The new graduation date is now November 24, 2029, postponed from November 24, 2026. Nepal also received the same extension following a draft resolution adopted by the Group of 77 and China.

The government plans to use this additional time to attract investment, expand market access for local goods, and enhance port efficiency. Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir emphasized continued efforts to sign trade deals with various countries and blocs.

Prime Minister’s adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir stated that the government is developing a transition strategy. Priorities include entering the trillion-dollar economy club, diversifying exports, and boosting productivity in vital sectors.

Economist Mustafizur Rahman of CPD called the extension "critically important," highlighting the opportunity to shift towards an investment and competition-driven economy. He stressed the need to cut business costs and improve the overall business environment.

Major trading partners, such as the European Union, are expected to extend their preparatory periods accordingly. Rahman also suggested developing promising sectors like pharmaceuticals, not solely relying on ready-made garments.

BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan welcomed the news but noted remaining challenges. He urged infrastructure development and key reforms to ensure local industries can compete in the EU market even after tariffs are reinstated.

Mohammad Abdur Razzaque of RAPID emphasized that while the extension provides valuable time, "time by itself will not improve our readiness." He called for urgent action from both government and the private sector with clear responsibilities and deadlines.

Restoring macroeconomic stability, particularly bringing down persistently high inflation, is crucial to protect export competitiveness. Securing a trade arrangement with the EU, Bangladesh’s largest export market, should be an early priority for greater business certainty.

Export diversification and rationalizing the tariff structure are also key priorities. The government should use the remaining LDC flexibilities to support new export sectors and encourage investment and competitiveness.
